title: In silico study of the potential of curcumin and its derivatives for increasing wild-type p53 expression and improving the function of p53 mutant R273H.
authors: Nainggolan, Sarah Ika; Rajuddin, Rajuddin; Kamarlis, Reno Keumalazia; Hambal, Muhammad; Frengki, Frengki
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过QSAR、分子对接和MD模拟评估姜黄素衍生物对p53突变体R273H的稳定作用，虽涉及蛋白-DNA结合域突变，但核心是药物-蛋白互作而非TF-DNA结合机制，方法可迁移性有限。
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIM: p53 is a critical tumor suppressor protein responsible for regulating the cell cycle and inducing apoptosis. Mutations in the p53 gene, particularly in the DNA-binding domain, are frequently associated with various cancers due to the loss of transcriptional activity. Curcumin and its derivatives have demonstrated potential as p53 enhancers and reactivators of mutant p53. This study employs in silico methods to evaluate the potential of curcumin derivatives to enhance wild-type p53 expression and restore the function of the p53 mutant R273H. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Curcumin and 20 derivatives were selected from PubChem for computational analysis. Their potential as p53 enhancers was assessed using Quantitative Structure-Activity Relationship (QSAR) analysis. Molecular docking was conducted to determine their binding affinities with wild-type and mutant p53 proteins, followed by molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to evaluate ligand-receptor stability. Pharmacokinetics and toxicity assessments were performed using predictive computational models to evaluate their drug-like properties. RESULTS: QSAR analysis identified hexahydrocurcumin (probable activity [Pa]: 0.837) and tetrahydrocurcumin (Pa: 0.752) as the most potent p53 enhancers. Molecular docking revealed strong binding affinities for curcumin derivatives at key p53 binding residues, particularly through hydrogen bonds with His 273 of the R273H mutant. MD simulations demonstrated that curcumin, bisdemethoxycurcumin, and monodemethylcurcumin stabilized p53 mutant R273H, closely mimicking the structural stability of wild-type p53. Pharmacokinetic analysis indicated favorable absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion profiles for most derivatives, with low toxicity predicted for the majority. CONCLUSION: Curcumin and its derivatives exhibit dual functions as p53 enhancers and reactivators of the p53 mutant R273H. Hexahydrocurcumin and tetrahydrocurcumin emerged as promising compounds with strong bioactivity and favorable pharmacokinetic properties, suggesting their potential as anticancer agents. Further in vitro and in vivo studies are necessary to validate these findings and explore their therapeutic applications.
abstract_zh: 背景与目的：p53是一种关键的肿瘤抑制蛋白，负责调控细胞周期并诱导凋亡。p53基因的突变，尤其是DNA结合域中的突变，常因转录活性丧失而与多种癌症相关。姜黄素及其衍生物已显示出作为p53增强剂和突变型p53再激活剂的潜力。本研究采用计算机模拟方法评估姜黄素衍生物增强野生型p53表达及恢复p53突变体R273H功能的潜力。材料与方法：从PubChem中选取姜黄素及20种衍生物进行计算分析。通过定量构效关系（QSAR）分析评估其作为p53增强剂的潜力。进行分子对接以确定其与野生型和突变型p53蛋白的结合亲和力，随后采用分子动力学（MD）模拟评估配体-受体稳定性。使用预测性计算模型进行药代动力学和毒性评估，以评价其类药性质。结果：QSAR分析确定六氢姜黄素（可能活性[Pa]：0.837）和四氢姜黄素（Pa：0.752）为最有效的p53增强剂。分子对接显示姜黄素衍生物在p53关键结合残基处具有强结合亲和力，尤其是通过与R273H突变体的His 273形成氢键。MD模拟表明，姜黄素、双去甲氧基姜黄素和单去甲基姜黄素稳定了p53突变体R273H，其结构稳定性与野生型p53高度相似。药代动力学分析显示大多数衍生物具有有利的吸收、分布、代谢和排泄特征，且多数预测毒性较低。结论：姜黄素及其衍生物表现出双重功能，既作为p53增强剂，又作为p53突变体R273H的再激活剂。六氢姜黄素和四氢姜黄素成为具有强生物活性和良好药代动力学特性的有前景化合物，提示其作为抗癌药物的潜力。需进一步开展体外和体内研究以验证这些发现并探索其治疗应用。
